transcript.speaker: Ethan Johnson
transcript.content: Hey Ben—can I ask you something a bit odd? Lately I've been having a streak of bad luck and I think it might be because of an old pendant I've been carrying. Could you take a look and help me figure out how to get rid of whatever's attached to it?

transcript.speaker: Benjamin Jackson
transcript.content: Of course—bring it over and I’ll take a look. I don’t believe in curses, but I get that the ritual could help you feel better, so I’ll help with a simple, safe cleansing: we can clean it (soap/salt water), leave it in sunlight for a bit, then do a short symbolic ritual where you say what you want to let go of before we tuck it away or bury it for a day—whatever feels right. When can you meet?

transcript.speaker: Ethan Johnson
transcript.content: Thanks, Ben — I really appreciate it. It’s a small silver pendant with a faint, odd engraving; I started having bad luck right after I picked it up. I’m free now and can meet at the fountain bench in 20 minutes, or tonight around 7 if that’s easier—what works for you?

transcript.speaker: Benjamin Jackson
transcript.content: 20 minutes works — meet you at the fountain bench. Bring the pendant; I’ll bring a small bowl, salt, soap and a cloth. We’ll do the quick clean, a bit of sunlight, then the short symbolic letting-go ritual you prefer. See you there.

transcript.speaker: Ethan Johnson
transcript.content: Perfect—thanks, Ben. I’ll be there in 20 minutes with the pendant. Do you want me to bring anything else (a small cloth or bag), or is what you’re bringing enough?

transcript.speaker: Benjamin Jackson
transcript.content: No need—what I’m bringing will do. If you have a small cloth or bag and want to keep the pendant after, bring it, but otherwise just bring the pendant and yourself. See you at the fountain bench in 20.

transcript.speaker: Ethan Johnson
transcript.content: Thanks, Ben — I’ll be there in 20 minutes with the pendant and a small cloth. See you at the fountain bench.

transcript.speaker: Benjamin Jackson
transcript.content: Great—see you at the fountain bench in 20. I’ll be the one with a small bowl; we’ll do the quick salt-and-sun clean and a short symbolic letting-go so you can feel lighter.

transcript.speaker: Ethan Johnson
transcript.content: I’m on my way—should be there in about 15 minutes. I’ll bring the pendant wrapped in a small cloth. Thanks again, Ben; could we keep this between us?

transcript.speaker: Benjamin Jackson
transcript.content: Of course—this stays between us. See you at the fountain in about 15 minutes; I’ll have the bowl, salt and a cloth ready. We’ll keep it simple and quick so you feel lighter.

transcript.speaker: Ethan Johnson
transcript.content: Hey Ben—I'm here at the fountain bench. I wrapped the pendant in this small cloth; can you take a look? And thanks again for keeping this between us.

transcript.speaker: Benjamin Jackson
transcript.content: Sure—mind if I unwrap it and take a closer look? This stays between us, and if you’re ready we can do the quick salt-and-sun clean now; do you want to say anything out loud for the letting-go ritual or have me guide you through it?

transcript.speaker: Ethan Johnson
transcript.content: Please unwrap it. I'd like you to guide me through the letting-go ritual — I don't really know what to say. If you notice anything odd about the engraving, tell me. Thanks, Ben.

transcript.speaker: Benjamin Jackson
transcript.content: Okay — I’ll unwrap it and take a look. The engraving looks like a small stylized spiral or knot, more decorative than anything overtly strange; there’s no obvious residue or damage. Here’s the plan: I’ll wash it gently with a little soap and a pinch of salt, rinse and dry it, then we’ll leave it in the sun for 10–15 minutes. After that, hold the pendant in your hands and say aloud what you want to let go of (a phrase like “I release bad luck” or name the feeling) three times, then tuck it back in the cloth or bury it for a day — short and symbolic, but it can help you feel lighter. Sound good?

transcript.speaker: Ethan Johnson
transcript.content: That sounds good — let’s do the wash and sunlight. Afterward I’d prefer to bury it for a day rather than keep it. I’m ready; please guide me through the words.

transcript.speaker: Benjamin Jackson
transcript.content: Alright — hold the pendant in your hands, close your eyes if it helps, and take three slow, deep breaths. When you're ready, say aloud a short phrase like 'I release this burden; I let go of bad luck' (or pick words that feel right to you) three times, pausing and breathing out after each repetition — I can count for you if you want. Then tuck it back in the cloth and we’ll bury it in a quiet patch of soil for a day; we’ll mark the spot and dig it up together tomorrow.

transcript.speaker: Ethan Johnson
transcript.content: Alright — I’m holding it and closing my eyes. Please count me through it; when you say go I’ll repeat: “I release this burden; I let go of bad luck” three times.

transcript.speaker: Benjamin Jackson
transcript.content: Okay — eyes closed, take three slow breaths with me. Ready? 1 — say: "I release this burden; I let go of bad luck." (breathe out). 2 — say it again. 3 — say it one more time. Good — tuck it in the cloth and we’ll bury it together.

transcript.speaker: Ethan Johnson
transcript.content: Thanks, Ben — I’ll tuck it back in. Let’s bury it in that quiet patch under the plane tree on the north side of the fountain; I can dig a shallow spot and mark it with a small stone. I really appreciate you doing this with me — ready when you are.

transcript.speaker: Benjamin Jackson
transcript.content: Alright — let’s bury it under the plane tree. I’ll help dig a shallow spot (just a few inches), tuck the cloth-wrapped pendant in, and we’ll mark it with a small stone; we’ll come back tomorrow to unearth it together. Ready when you are.
